quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'No sooner' at the front flips the auxiliary and subject, and 'than' introduces what happened right after.
quests.explanation: 'No sooner' + 'had' + subject (we) + past participle (sat down) + 'than' + sudden event (the fire alarm went off). 'No sooner...than' emphasizes how quickly one event followed another.
quests.textToSpeak: No sooner had we sat down than the fire alarm went off.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'Hardly' also triggers inversion, and 'when' replaces 'than' in this version.
quests.explanation: 'Hardly' + 'had' + subject (she) + past participle (finished speaking) + 'when' + sudden event (the questions began). 'Hardly...when' works just like 'no sooner...than' for near-instant sequencing.
quests.textToSpeak: Hardly had she finished speaking when the questions began.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: The pattern repeats: inversion first, then the interrupting event right after 'than'.
quests.explanation: 'No sooner' + 'had' + subject (the meeting) + past participle (ended) + 'than' + sudden event (a new problem appeared). This structure is common for describing frustratingly quick turnarounds.
quests.textToSpeak: No sooner had the meeting ended than a new problem appeared.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'However' plus an adjective opens the sentence, before the rest of the clause follows.
quests.explanation: 'However' + adjective (difficult) + clause ('it may be') + main clause ('we have to address this now'). 'However' plus an adjective concedes a difficulty before stating a firm decision anyway.
quests.textToSpeak: However difficult it may be, we have to address this now.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: The adjective 'tempting' leads, describing the offer before the main action follows.
quests.explanation: 'However' + adjective (tempting) + clause ('the offer seemed') + main clause (she turned it down). This concedes the offer's appeal before revealing the surprising decision.
quests.textToSpeak: However tempting the offer seemed, she turned it down.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: This time an adverb, not an adjective, follows 'however' — the pattern still works the same way.
quests.explanation: 'However' + adverb (carefully) + clause ('we planned') + main clause ('something always went wrong'). 'However' can precede an adverb as well as an adjective in this concessive structure.
quests.textToSpeak: However carefully we planned, something always went wrong.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: One embedded clause sits inside another — a reported suggestion, tucked inside a 'why' question.
quests.explanation: Subject (Nobody) + 'could explain' + 'why' + embedded clause ('the system had suggested that we restart it', itself containing a reported clause). Embedded structures can nest inside each other, layer by layer.
quests.textToSpeak: Nobody could explain why the system had suggested that we restart it.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: Two embedded questions stack: 'whether' leads to a clause that itself contains 'what'.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + 'wasn't sure' + 'whether' + embedded clause ('the client understood what the delay actually meant', itself containing an embedded 'what' clause). One embedded question can contain a second embedded question inside it.
quests.textToSpeak: She wasn't sure whether the client understood what the delay actually meant.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'How' introduces a clause that itself contains a 'who' clause — two layers of uncertainty.
quests.explanation: Subject (I) + 'still don't know' + 'how' + embedded clause ('they decided who would lead the negotiation', itself containing an embedded 'who' clause). Two embedded questions can nest together in natural, spoken English.
quests.textToSpeak: I still don't know how they decided who would lead the negotiation.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: Two separate perfect-modal-passive phrases appear in one sentence, joined by a relative clause.
quests.explanation: Subject (The changes) + relative clause (', which should have been implemented months ago,') + main clause ('still haven't been finalized'). Two different passive perfect structures can describe the same subject from two angles.
quests.textToSpeak: The changes, which should have been implemented months ago, still haven't been finalized.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: The relative clause carries its own passive perfect modal, separate from the main clause's passive verb.
quests.explanation: Subject (A decision) + relative clause ('that could have been avoided') + main clause ('was ultimately forced upon the team', passive). The relative clause and the main clause each carry their own passive structure.
quests.textToSpeak: A decision that could have been avoided was ultimately forced upon the team.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: A concessive clause interrupts the sentence, carrying its own dense passive modal phrase.
quests.explanation: Subject (The issue) + inserted clause (', although it should have been resolved earlier,') + verb (remains) + adjective (unaddressed). The inserted concessive clause itself contains a full passive perfect modal.
quests.textToSpeak: The issue, although it should have been resolved earlier, remains unaddressed.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: The 'if' clause's subject is itself a whole nominal relative clause: 'what she said'.
quests.explanation: 'If' + condition ('what she said turns out to be true', containing a nominal relative subject) + result (the entire plan will need revising). A conditional's condition can itself contain a nominal relative clause.
quests.textToSpeak: If what she said turns out to be true, the entire plan will need revising.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'Unless' leads into a condition that itself contains an embedded 'why' question.
quests.explanation: 'Unless' + condition ('someone can explain why the numbers don't match', containing an embedded question) + result ('we can't move forward'). 'Unless' clauses can carry their own embedded question inside them.
quests.textToSpeak: Unless someone can explain why the numbers don't match, we can't move forward.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: The unreal past condition contains its own embedded 'what' clause as the object of 'mentioned'.
quests.explanation: 'If' + unreal past condition ('the report hadn't mentioned what went wrong', containing an embedded clause) + unreal past result ('nobody would have noticed'). Third conditional clauses can also carry embedded questions inside them.
quests.textToSpeak: If the report hadn't mentioned what went wrong, nobody would have noticed.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'She' and 'herself' both refer back to the intern, not the manager — listen carefully for who is doing what.
quests.explanation: Subject (The manager) + verb (told) + object (the intern) + 'that' + reported clause ('she would need to redo the analysis herself'). Pronouns like 'she' and 'herself' here both refer to 'the intern', the closer noun.
quests.textToSpeak: The manager told the intern that she would need to redo the analysis herself.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'He' and 'his' could refer to either person — context alone tells you it's the supplier defending himself.
quests.explanation: 'When' + time clause (the client called the supplier) + main clause ('he insisted the delay wasn't his fault'). Without more context, 'he' most naturally refers to the closer noun, 'the supplier'.
quests.textToSpeak: When the client called the supplier, he insisted the delay wasn't his fault.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: Both instances of 'she' refer to the student, not the teacher, despite the teacher being mentioned first.
quests.explanation: 'Although' + contrast (the teacher praised the student) + main clause ('she still felt she could have done better'). Both 'she' pronouns here refer to 'the student', the sentence's true focus.
quests.textToSpeak: Although the teacher praised the student, she still felt she could have done better.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'Reconvene' formally means 'meet again', and 'once' introduces the trigger for that future meeting.
quests.explanation: Subject (The board) + 'will reconvene' + 'once' + condition ('the audit findings have been fully reviewed', present perfect passive). This formal sentence links a future meeting to the completion of a review process.
quests.textToSpeak: The board will reconvene once the audit findings have been fully reviewed.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'Caution that' introduces a careful warning, common in academic writing.
quests.explanation: Subject (Researchers) + verb (caution) + 'that' + embedded clause ('the results should not be generalized beyond this sample', passive). 'Caution that' warns readers against overinterpreting a finding.
quests.textToSpeak: Researchers caution that the results should not be generalized beyond this sample.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'Exploring alternatives' shows an ongoing search, and the relative clause explains the goal of that search.
quests.explanation: Subject (Management) + 'is exploring' + object (alternatives) + relative clause ('that might reduce long-term operational risk'). The relative clause explains the purpose behind the ongoing search.
quests.textToSpeak: Management is exploring alternatives that might reduce long-term operational risk.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: Two past perfect events compete for 'earliest' — listen for which one truly finished first.
quests.explanation: 'By the time' + time clause ('she'd read the report twice', past perfect) + main clause ('the meeting it was written for had already ended', also past perfect). Both clauses use past perfect, but the main clause's event finished even earlier.
quests.textToSpeak: By the time she'd read the report twice, the meeting it was written for had already ended.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: The participle opener sets up a past event that shapes the team's present awareness.
quests.explanation: 'Having already missed one deadline' (participle opener) + main clause ('the team knew a second delay would be unacceptable'). The participle clause explains the past experience behind the team's current concern.
quests.textToSpeak: Having already missed one deadline, the team knew a second delay would be unacceptable.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: A relative clause sits inside the time clause, both leading up to the slow recovery described at the end.
quests.explanation: 'Once' + time clause ('the issue that had been overlooked was finally addressed', containing a relative clause) + result ('confidence slowly returned'). The relative clause explains why the issue took so long to resolve.
quests.textToSpeak: Once the issue that had been overlooked was finally addressed, confidence slowly returned.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'As' here means 'while', not 'because' — listen for the parallel timing, not a cause.
quests.explanation: 'As' (meaning 'while') + time clause (the deadline approached) + main clause ('the pressure the team felt only grew', with an omitted relative clause). 'As' can mean 'while' or 'because' depending on context.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'For all' here means 'despite', an unusual but natural concessive use of 'for'.
quests.explanation: 'For all' (meaning 'despite') + factor (his experience) + main clause ('he still made a basic mistake'). 'For all' is an idiomatic way of saying 'despite', not its usual meaning of 'because of'.
quests.textToSpeak: For all his experience, he still made a basic mistake.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'That' is omitted after 'claims' — the reported clause follows directly, without the connecting word.
quests.explanation: Subject (The report) + verb (claims) + reported clause (the results, though promising, leave several questions unanswered, 'that' omitted). Dropping 'that' after reporting verbs is very common and natural in spoken English.
quests.textToSpeak: The report claims the results, though promising, leave several questions unanswered.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: The inversion structure returns, but now with an inserted phrase describing the new problem.
quests.explanation: 'No sooner' + 'had' + subject (the team) + past participle ('addressed one issue') + 'than' + subject (another) + inserted phrase (', seemingly unrelated,') + verb (problem emerged). An inserted phrase can interrupt even a tightly structured inversion sentence.
quests.textToSpeak: No sooner had the team addressed one issue than another, seemingly unrelated, problem emerged.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: A concessive inversion opens, and a relative clause with its own passive modal follows in the result.
quests.explanation: 'However' + adverb (thoroughly) + clause ('the report had been reviewed', passive) + main clause ('something that should have been caught was still missed', containing its own relative clause). Two dense structures combine to describe a frustrating oversight.
quests.textToSpeak: However thoroughly the report had been reviewed, something that should have been caught was still missed.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: A nominal relative clause sits inside the 'unless' condition, just as it did earlier with 'if'.
quests.explanation: 'Unless' + condition ('what the client described turns out to be inaccurate', containing a nominal relative subject) + result ('the entire timeline will need to be reconsidered', passive). This mirrors the earlier 'if what she said' pattern, now used with 'unless'.
quests.textToSpeak: Unless what the client described turns out to be inaccurate, the entire timeline will need to be reconsidered.
